progressionAssessment.rationale: Sustainability, philosophy and imperial history foundations precede archaeology, material-culture, landscape and digital methods. ENSGATE101 precedes Earth Observation, the only formal prerequisite within the programme. Introductory archaeology, art history, literature and data work precede advanced heritage, museum, media and research courses. All courses occur in their exact planned terms; seven are at 300 level.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two complete related-fields programmes are defensible. The first studies ancient societies and material culture through UCR archaeology, history, art, landscape and research courses; the second is a distinct public-heritage and museum route. The next generator-backed direction—excavation, archaeological science and bioarchaeology—cannot be implemented at UCR, so production stops at two.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce archaeological interpretation of material evidence and past societies.
Both study Greek material evidence. The UCR course focuses on Greek community and democracy.
Groningen offers a dedicated regional survey of Northwest Europe.
Groningen studies the history and theory of archaeological and anthropological interpretation.
Groningen offers a dedicated study of Arctic cultures.
Groningen advances from introductory archaeology to specialist analysis of artifacts. UCR introduces related methods through craft and material culture.
Groningen uses archaeological evidence to examine social change. UCR studies related questions through the history of empires.
Groningen introduces the study of biological remains in archaeological contexts.
Groningen studies archaeological materials, conservation and scientific measurement.
Groningen students take part in an excavation and report on their findings.
Both use GIS and spatial data. UCR applies them to environmental observation.
Groningen analyzes plant remains as archaeological evidence.
Groningen analyzes animal remains as archaeological evidence.
Groningen studies human skeletal remains.
Groningen combines geoarchaeology with a second fieldwork course. UCR’s soils course develops complementary earth-science methods.
Groningen brings together evidence from several branches of bioarchaeology.
Both connect the classical past to heritage. UCR focuses on ancient democracy.
Groningen applies archaeological theory to contemporary questions.
Groningen develops archaeological research design and digital analysis. UCR teaches general data and research methods.
Groningen requires a thesis in archaeology. UCR shows optional independent research separately.

Choose a faculty-wide course in humane AI, narrative, global change or cultural heritage.
